memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "I give you all the finest olive oil and all the finest new wine and grain they give the Lord as the firstfruits of their harvest. All the land's firstfruits that they bring to the Lord will be yours. Everyone in your household who is ceremonially clean may eat it." — Num 18:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gives the priests "the finest" oil, wine, and grain — the firstfruits, the very best of the harvest. The people brought their first and finest to God, and God shared it with those who served Him. Nothing second-rate was offered to the Lord, and so nothing second-rate was given to His servants.

This reveals God's worthiness. He is deserving of the best we have, not the leftovers. When Israel brought firstfruits, they were declaring that God comes first, before their own needs and wants. Giving God the first and finest was an act of trust and honour, saying, "You are worthy of my best, and I trust You to provide the rest."

We are invited to the same posture of heart. Do we give God the first of our time, energy, and resources, or only what remains after everything else has had its claim? Offering God our best is not about earning His favour — it is about honouring His supreme worth and trusting His faithful care. What we put first shows where our heart truly rests.

And how could we hold back our best from the God who gave His very best for us? He did not send an angel or spare from His abundance; He gave His only Son, holding nothing back. Christ is God's firstfruits of love poured out for us. In grateful response, we gladly offer Him the first and finest of our lives, not to gain His blessing, but because He has already given us everything in Jesus.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you give God your first and finest, or your leftovers?
2. What would it look like to honour God's worth with your best this week?
3. How does God giving His best in Christ shape your response to Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are worthy of my very best, not my leftovers. Teach me to honour You with the first and finest of my life, and to trust You with the rest. Thank You that You gave Your best in Christ, holding nothing back. Amen.
